title: File Type Control actions, direction and defaults

prose.text: Caution for traffic with no user to acknowledge is open {{gap:caution-without-a-user}}, and the fate of unscannable or unknown files that no rule names is open {{gap:unscannable-and-unknown-default}}.

FTP Control has no action selector of its own; see [[zia.ftp-control.settings]]. {{ftp-via-protocol-criterion}} See [[zia.file-type-control.api-shape]] for the wire values. How the criteria decide a match is in [[zia.file-type-control.criteria]], and where File Type Control sits relative to DLP and scanning is in [[zia.file-type-control.pipeline]].

checks.do: Whether a Caution rule applies to traffic with no user to acknowledge it.
Whether an unscannable or unknown file is allowed or blocked when no rule names it.

default-allow-all.statement: By default the service allows upload and download of all file types. File Type Control restricts that; Zscaler also publishes a recommended policy. A newly added rule's status is Disabled until it is enabled.

quotes: By default, the Zscaler service allows the upload and download of all file types.
Zscaler also has a recommended policy for File Type Control.
Use the File Type Control policy to restrict the upload and download of various types of files.
Rule Status: By default, the status is Disabled.

actions.statement: A rule's action is Allow, Caution or Block. Caution displays a warning before the service lets the user perform the action. A block displays a notification whose content is set on the End User Notification page.

quotes: When you choose the Caution action, the Zscaler service displays a warning before it allows the user to perform the action.
The content of the block notification is configured in the End User Notification page.
Action: Choose to Allow, Block, or Caution users from uploading or downloading files.

browser-notification-template.statement: A browser notification template can be selected for the rule; the field appears only when the action is Caution or Block.

quotes: This field appears when the application access is set to either Caution or Block.

Browser Notification Template: (Optional) Select a browser-based EUN message from the drop-down menu to display the message in the browser when the user activity triggers the File Type Control Policy rule.

operation.statement: Each rule's action applies to uploads, downloads or both, so a file type can be allowed one way and blocked the other.

quotes: Upload/Download: Choose whether the specified action applies to uploading files, downloading files, or both.
You can allow, caution or block uploading, downloading or both.

capture-on-block.statement: When Traffic Capture is enabled, the Capture option appears for rules whose action is Block, and captured traffic is stored as PCAP files.

quotes: If Traffic Capture is enabled, the Capture option appears when Block is selected.
Captured traffic is stored in PCAP files for later analysis.

disabled-rules-hold-order.statement: Disabled rules can hold a rule order; evaluation skips them and moves to the next rule. A rule can carry an expiration, after which it keeps its place in the order but is not evaluated.

quotes: During evaluation, the service skips the disabled rules and moves to the successive ones.
The rule retains its place in the rule order but is not evaluated after it expires.

ftp-via-protocol-criterion.statement: A File Type Control rule's Protocols criterion includes FTP over HTTP (files from FTP over HTTP websites) and Native FTP (files from native FTP servers); both require a Firewall subscription.

quotes: Files from FTP over HTTP websites. (Requires Firewall subscription.)
Files from native FTP servers. (Requires Firewall subscription.)

caution-without-a-user.title: Caution for traffic with no interactive user
caution-without-a-user.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'CAUTION is user-interactive. For API-only or headless flows (cloud workloads, CI runners), CAUTION effectively = BLOCK because there's no user to acknowledge.' The vendor says Caution displays a warning before allowing the action; it does not say what happens when no browser can display it. Resolves with a lab test from a non-browser client.
caution-without-a-user.blocks: choosing Caution versus Block for programmatic traffic

unscannable-and-unknown-default.title: Fail-open or fail-closed for unscannable and unknown files
unscannable-and-unknown-default.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Default action for unscannables is a tenant choice: fail-open or fail-closed' and 'File Type Control on unidentifiable files is a tenant decision ... No middle ground without writing explicit rules.' The vendor documents Unscannable Files and Undetectable File as rule criteria, so an admin can write rules for them; it does not describe a separate Unscannable Files policy or a tenant-level fail-open setting. With no matching rule the default is allow all (claim default-allow-all). Resolves with the console's Unscannable Files option, if one exists, or a lab test.
unscannable-and-unknown-default.blocks: advising what happens to unscannable files with no explicit rule
